summary: All four registered obligations are now disposed with no pending work: three confirmed in-scope violations (claim-truncate-store-failure-watermark, claim-snapshot-install-stale-watermark, claim-snapshot-trigger-underflow) and one reviewed bounded no-violation (claim-config-rollback-consistency), with review_issues empty. New obligation capacity is exhausted, so this step uses the remaining authorized source work instead of manufacturing a placeholder: submission is action=research carrying draft/map.json plus one map change and sourced feedback that resolves a boundary the confirmed truncation-failure finding had left open. The trace: replicateTo lowers nextIndex with max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1), so the follower's stale LastLog clamps nextIndex above its real log end; setupAppendEntries sets PrevLogEntry=0 once nextIndex reaches 1 and setNewLogs reads the leader's own store, so an error - and therefore the SEND_SNAP fallback - only occurs when the leader's log itself is missing an index. With the leader still holding the log, every attempt is rejected by the follower at the index it no longer holds and nextIndex converges to 1, so no snapshot is sent and the follower stays a divergent voter until it restarts. The map change refines Fact F-log-watermark (impact meaning, since validity_context is structural): its validity statement now records the two confirmed runtime failures of the condition with their check ids, and its second unknown is narrowed to the variant that remains genuinely open - a leader whose own log has been compacted below the failure point, which routes into the snapshot path and interacts with the installSnapshot finding. Two preflight iterations were needed and are recorded honestly in the product bytes: the map base version had to match the accepted v2, and the change impact had to be meaning rather than clarification because validity_context is a structural field. Feedback cites F-log-watermark, the claim and the executed artifact plus the replication source ranges, states explicitly that this is a sourced reading of the recovery consumer rather than new execution evidence, and lists the remaining open boundaries (the compacted-leader variant, installSnapshot reachability and its non-monotonic branch, and the unmeasured follow-on of the snapshot-trigger underflow). Preflight validation now returns valid with no diagnostics.
